## Package Overview
The package provides a comprehensive toolkit to process, explore, and map historical timelines from the NOAA Global Significant Earthquake Database. It includes functions to clean raw spatial attributes, display stratified event timelines via `ggplot2`, and compile interactive tracking maps using `leaflet`.

## 1. Data Processing and Cleaning
Before generating visualizations, your raw earthquake source strings must be run through the programmatic sanitization engine:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(readr)

# Read the raw NOAA data
raw_data <- readr::read_delim("signif.txt", delim = "\t")

# Clean coordinates, reconstruct calendar dates, and format location text
cleaned_df <- raw_data %>% 
  eq_clean_data() %>% 
  eq_location_clean()
```
## 2. Chronological Visualization (Module 2)
You can compare earthquake time distributions grouped by country. Marker nodes map earthquake intensity to size and total fatalities to color scales:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
timeline_df <- cleaned_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(YEAR >= 2000, YEAR <= 2015, COUNTRY %in% c("CHINA", "JAPAN", "USA"))

ggplot(timeline_df, aes(x = DATE, y = COUNTRY, size = EQ_PRIMARY, colour = TOTAL_DEATHS)) +
  geom_timeline() +
  geom_timeline_label(aes(label = LOCATION_NAME, magnitude = EQ_PRIMARY), n_max = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 3. Interactive Leaflet Maps (Module 3)
Finally, you can construct an interactive map with multi-variable boldface HTML popup description panels:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
map_df <- cleaned_df %>% 
  dplyr::filter(COUNTRY == "MEXICO" & lubridate::year(DATE) >= 2000) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(popup_text = eq_create_label(.))

eq_map(map_df, annot_col = "popup_text")
```
